Committee: Insurance
Sponsor: Rich
Analyst: Robin Rawls
Date: 04/27/2021
FISCAL NOTE
House Bill 612 as introduced authorizes the Commissioner of Insurance to (1) establish a state health insurance exchange for the purchase and sale of qualified individual health insurance plans and (2) establish a reinsurance program, pursuant to a federal waiver.
The bill could increase the administrative obligations of the Department of Insurance by an undetermined amount to: 1) adopt rules regarding operation of the exchange and reinsurance program, 2) enforce compliance with state and federal laws relating to the exchange, 3) apply for waivers and funding and to expend grants and funds behalf of the exchange and reinsurance program, and 4) operate the state health insurance exchange and reinsurance program.
These obligations could be offset, in whole or in part, by the user fees, set by the commissioner, that may be assessed and collected on monthly premiums of health insurance plans offered on the exchange, up to the amount necessary to operate the exchange and reinsurance program.
According to the Department of Insurance, 166,973 policies were purchased on the current federal health insurance exchange by Alabama residents for 2021, which generated approximately $1.5 billion annualized state premium. The current 3% federal user fee generates an estimated $45 million annually from these plans purchased on the federal exchange.
The bill further establishes the Alabama Health Insurance Exchange Fund and the reinsurance fund within the State Treasury to be used for the administration of the Alabama Health Insurance Exchange and reinsurance program, respectively.
Kerry Rich, Chair
